predecessors.name: Myinsaing Kingdom
predecessors.text: "the entire Irrawaddy valley between Prome in the south and Tagaung in the north", Upper Burma "from Tagaung to Tharrawaddy"

successors.name: Sagaing Kingdom
successors.text: Pinya less the Toungoo district that broke away in 1358; "He took Pinya in September 1364" (Thado Minbya of Sagaing)

ledger.x: 7 February 1313: Thihathu is crowned king and founds the capital Pinya.
1315: Prince Saw Yun, governor of Sagaing, breaks with his father.
1317: Saw Yun's fight for autonomy ends in his favour ("fought for autonomy in 1315-17"); "Sagaing got a breather in 1317 when Toungoo and Taungdwin revolted".
1317: Sagaing is left autonomous under Pinya's nominal overlordship.
1325: Sagaing formally secedes after Thihathu's death.
September 1364: Thado Minbya of Sagaing takes Pinya.
September 1364: the Pinya Kingdom ends when Thado Minbya takes the city; he founds Ava in 1365 ("founded the Ava kingdom in 1365").

wars.name: Saw Yun's war of autonomy (Sagaing)
wars.outcome: Saw Yun "successfully fought for autonomy in 1315-17" and Sagaing seceded formally in 1325 after Thihathu's death.

wars.name: Raids on Pinya's southern vassals (Ramanya 1330, Arakan 1333-34)
wars.outcome: "Ramanya attacked Prome in 1330; Arakan raided Thayet in 1333-34"; the page records no change of border.

wars.name: Sagaing-Pinya hostilities and the 1351 truce
wars.outcome: Sagaing's 1339 expedition to Mindon, inside Pinya territory, brought Saw Yun's children back to Sagaing (Sagaing page); Kyawswa II "agreed to a truce with the northern rival in 1351".

wars.name: Maw Shan raids on Sagaing and Pinya
wars.outcome: "Two Maw raids in 1358-59 and 1362-63 thoroughly devastated Pinya's countryside"; "The Maw forces sacked Sagaing in April 1364" and "sacked the city in May" (Pinya); no Shan land was added.

wars.name: Thado Minbya's conquest of Pinya
wars.outcome: "He took Pinya in September 1364"; Thado Minbya "claimed himself king of Sagaing and Pinya" and founded Ava in 1365.

certainty.note: No surveyed or treaty border: "The majority of the vassal states reported in the chronicles lay within a 250 km radius from Pinya", and "Pinya's effective power extended no more than 150 km from Pinya".
